title.value: Randomized Trial of Verubecestat for Prodromal Alzheimer’s Disease
title.quote: Randomized Trial of Verubecestat for Prodromal Alzheimer’s Disease

design.value: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel group, 104-week trial period (part 1), followed by an optional extension period (part 2); conducted at 238 centers in 22 countries from November 2013 through April 2018
design.quote: The trial consisted of a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel group, 104-week trial period (part 1), followed by an optional extension period with a planned duration of up to 5 years (part 2).

n.quote: A total of 1454 patients were enrolled; 485 were randomly assigned to receive oral verubecestat at a dose of 12 mg per day (the 12-mg group)

n_description.value: 1454 patients enrolled and randomly assigned 1:1:1 — 485 to verubecestat 12 mg/day, 484 to verubecestat 40 mg/day, 485 to matching placebo; efficacy analyses used a modified intention-to-treat population whose per-group numbers differed from the randomized numbers
n_description.quote: The number of patients in each group in the modified intention-to-treat population differed from the number of patients who were randomly assigned to a trial group () because of differences in the numbers of missing data in each group.

population.value: Patients aged 50 to 85 years with prodromal Alzheimer's disease — memory impairment (subjective memory decline for at least 1 year corroborated by an informant, RBANS Delayed Memory Index score of 85 or less) and elevated brain amyloid on PET, with MMSE 24 to 30, who did not meet criteria for dementia
population.quote: in patients who had memory impairment and elevated brain amyloid levels but whose condition did not meet the case definition of dementia

followup.value: 104 weeks (part 1), with an optional extension period of up to 5 years (part 2); the trial was terminated early and no patients completed the extension phase
followup.quote: We conducted a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 104-week trial to evaluate verubecestat at doses of 12 mg and 40 mg per day, as compared with placebo

intervention.value: Oral verubecestat (a BACE-1 inhibitor) at 12 mg per day or 40 mg per day, once daily, administered as identical-appearing tablets
intervention.quote: In part 1, patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive, once daily, oral verubecestat at a dose of 12 mg, oral verubecestat at a dose of 40 mg, or oral placebo.

comparator.value: Oral matching placebo, once daily (485 patients randomly assigned to receive matching placebo)
comparator.quote: In part 1, patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive, once daily, oral verubecestat at a dose of 12 mg, oral verubecestat at a dose of 40 mg, or oral placebo.

biomarker_confirmation.value: Brain amyloid confirmed by a radiologist's visual inspection of amyloid-ligand PET imaging; the diagnosis of prodromal Alzheimer's disease was confirmed by independent review
biomarker_confirmation.quote: the presence of brain amyloid as gauged by a radiologist’s visual inspection of amyloid-ligand positronemission tomography (PET) imaging

outcomes.name: Change from baseline to week 104 in the Clinical Dementia Rating Scale–Sum of Boxes score (CDR-SB)
outcomes.prespecification_evidence: The primary efficacy outcome was the change from baseline to week 104 in the Clinical Dementia Rating Scale–Sum of Boxes score (CDR-SB; scores range from 0 to 18
outcomes.effect_estimate: Model-based mean change from baseline to week 104: 1.65 in the 12-mg group, 2.02 in the 40-mg group, and 1.58 in the placebo group — the 40-mg group was worse than placebo
outcomes.p_value: P = 0.67 for the comparison between the 12-mg group and the placebo group and P = 0.01 for the comparison between the 40-mg group and the placebo group, favoring the placebo group
outcomes.quote: The model-based mean change score from baseline to week 104 in the CDR-SB score (the primary outcome) was 1.65 in the 12-mg group, 2.02 in the 40-mg group, and 1.58 in the placebo group

outcomes.name: Progression to the diagnosis of dementia due to Alzheimer’s disease
outcomes.prespecification_evidence: There were seven secondary outcomes: the progression to the diagnosis of dementia due to Alzheimer’s disease; the change from week 13 to week 104 in the CDR-SB score
outcomes.effect_estimate: 24.5 events per 100 patient-years in the 12-mg group, 25.5 in the 40-mg group, and 19.3 in the placebo group; hazard ratio 1.30 for 12 mg vs. placebo and hazard ratio 1.38 for 40 mg vs. placebo, favoring placebo
outcomes.confidence_interval: 97.51% confidence interval [CI], 1.01 to 1.68 (12 mg vs. placebo) and 97.51% CI, 1.07 to 1.79 (40 mg vs. placebo), unadjusted for multiple comparisons
outcomes.quote: The event rates for dementia due to Alzheimer’s disease per 100 patient-years were 24.5 in the 12-mg group, 25.5 in the 40-mg group, and 19.3 in the placebo group

outcomes.name: Change from week 13 to week 104 in the CDR-SB score
outcomes.prespecification_evidence: There were seven secondary outcomes: the progression to the diagnosis of dementia due to Alzheimer’s disease; the change from week 13 to week 104 in the CDR-SB score
outcomes.quote: The failure to support the primary hypothesis of superiority of verubecestat over placebo with respect to the CDR-SB score precluded formal statistical inferences for the remaining outcomes.

primary_endpoint_status.explanation: The primary outcome — change from baseline to week 104 in CDR-SB — showed no benefit of verubecestat over placebo (1.65 in the 12-mg group and 2.02 in the 40-mg group vs. 1.58 in the placebo group, P = 0.67 and P = 0.01 respectively), with the 40-mg comparison significantly favouring placebo, and the trial was terminated for futility.
primary_endpoint_status.quote: verubecestat showed no benefit with respect to the primary clinical outcome (a change in the CDR-SB score from baseline to week 104), as compared with placebo

multiplicity.approach: Bonferroni approach splitting the overall alpha between the two dose levels of verubecestat, in conjunction with a hierarchical sequential testing approach of outcomes; once superiority was not shown for the primary CDR-SB outcome, all subsequent outcomes were assumed not to have differed significantly and are reported as point estimates with 97.51% confidence intervals (95% for exploratory outcomes) not adjusted for multiple comparisons
multiplicity.quote: A Bonferroni approach (splitting the overall α between the two dose levels of verubecestat) in conjunction with a hierarchical sequential testing approach of outcomes was used to control for the type 1 error rate

conflicts: The sponsor (Merck Sharp & Dohme [MSD]) designed the trial in consultation with the academic authors; data were collected by the investigators and analyzed by the sponsor.
The first draft of the manuscript was written by the first author and a professional medical writer who was employed by the sponsor.
Confidentiality agreements were in place between the sponsor and the authors.
Multiple named authors and acknowledged contributors are identified as employees of MSD (e.g., pharmacokinetic analysis, administrative support, manuscript preparation and submission assistance).
The individual author disclosure statements themselves are not contained in this document: "Disclosure forms provided by the authors are available with the full text of this article at NEJM.org ."
limitations: The comparisons beyond the primary outcome are exploratory with unadjusted confidence intervals: "These comparisons are exploratory, and the confidence intervals are unadjusted; thus, the strength of any resulting inferences is limited."
The trial was not powered for time-point or subgroup analyses: "Analyses at other time points and subgroup anaIyses were prespecified, but the triaI was not powered for such anaIyses."

Early termination for futility meant far fewer completers than planned: "the number of patients who completed the trial at week 104 in each group (231 in the 12-mg group, 234 in the 40-mg group, and 239 patients in the placebo group) () was less than the 338 patients per group who had been expected to complete the trial."
No patients completed the extension phase: "None of the patients completed the extension phase because of the early termination"

The cerebrospinal fluid biomarker substudy was too small for its planned analyses: "Since there were few patients in the substudy of biomarkers in cerebrospinal fluid (five or six patients per group), planned analyses were not performed"

Formal statistical inference for outcomes after the primary was precluded by the hierarchical plan: "A formal statistical analysis was not performed because of the hierarchical analysis plan and failure to show superiority of the drug in the analysis of the primary outcome"
Earlier time-point findings are suggestive only: "suggesting but not confirming the possibility of worse performance at these earlier time points in the high-dose verubecestat group"

MRI surveillance for amyloid-related imaging abnormalities was discontinued during the trial: "MRI was initially performed to assess for possible amyloid-related imaging abnormalities but was subsequently discontinued on the basis of feedback from the independent monitoring committee and regulatory recommendations."

risk_of_bias.judgement: The sponsor designed the trial and analysed the data; the first manuscript draft was written with a sponsor-employed medical writer, and confidentiality agreements were in place between sponsor and authors.
risk_of_bias.quote: The sponsor (Merck Sharp & Dohme [MSD]) designed the trial in consultation with the academic authors. Data were collected by the investigators and analyzed by the sponsor.

risk_of_bias.judgement: Fewer than half of enrolled patients completed part 1, and completion numbers fell well short of the planned 338 per group because of the early stop.
risk_of_bias.quote: A total of 704 patients (47.7 to 49.3% of the patients in each group) completed part 1 of the trial

risk_of_bias.judgement: The trial was stopped about 12 months before scheduled completion of part 1 on the recommendation of the data and safety monitoring committee, reducing the information available for all outcomes.
risk_of_bias.quote: At the time of trial termination, enrollment had been completed and approximately 12 months remained before the scheduled completion of part 1.

risk_of_bias.judgement: After the primary outcome failed, the hierarchical gatekeeping plan precluded formal inference; all subsequent estimates are reported with unadjusted confidence intervals, which the paper itself says limits inference.
risk_of_bias.quote: Separately for each dose level, if significant superiority was not shown, all subsequent outcomes were assumed not to have differed significantly between the groups and are reported as point estimates with 97.51% confidence intervals

risk_of_bias.judgement: MRI surveillance for amyloid-related imaging abnormalities was stopped part-way through the trial, so the absence of ARIA is based on incomplete imaging follow-up.
risk_of_bias.quote: MRI was initially performed to assess for possible amyloid-related imaging abnormalities but was subsequently discontinued on the basis of feedback from the independent monitoring committee and regulatory recommendations.

risk_of_bias.judgement: The abstract and the Results section assign the 234 and 231 completer counts to different groups: the abstract reads 234, 231, 239 in the order 12-mg, 40-mg, placebo, while the Results text reads 231 in the 12-mg group and 234 in the 40-mg group.
risk_of_bias.quote: A total of 234 patients, 231 patients, and 239 patients per group, respectively, completed 104 weeks of the trial regimen.

disagreements.question: Does BACE-1 inhibition with verubecestat benefit patients with prodromal Alzheimer's disease?
disagreements.position: No. Verubecestat did not improve clinical ratings of dementia, and some measures suggested that cognition and daily function were worse with verubecestat than with placebo.
disagreements.attributed_to: This document (Egan et al., the trial investigators and sponsor Merck Sharp & Dohme)
disagreements.quote: Verubecestat did not improve clinical ratings of dementia among patients with prodromal Alzheimer’s disease, and some measures suggested that cognition and daily function were worse among patients who received verubecestat than among those who received placebo.

disagreements.question: Did verubecestat accelerate progression to dementia due to Alzheimer's disease?
disagreements.position: The hazard ratios for progression to dementia, whose confidence intervals excluded 1 and favoured placebo, suggest that verubecestat may have accelerated progression, although formal statistical analysis was not performed.
disagreements.quote: did not include 1, suggesting that verubecestat may have accelerated the progression to diagnosis of dementia due to Alzheimer’s disease

disagreements.question: Why do these results differ from the earlier verubecestat trial in mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's dementia, where no overall treatment effect was seen?
disagreements.position: Patients here were on average 3 to 4 years earlier in the disease course and patients at an earlier stage may be more sensitive to substantial BACE-1 inhibition, perhaps because of a role of BACE-1 in normal synaptic function; effects due to BACE-2 inhibition are also possible.
disagreements.quote: Patients at an earlier stage of the disease may be more sensitive to the effects of substantial BACE-1 inhibition, perhaps because of a role of BACE-1 in normal synaptic function.

disagreements.question: Did verubecestat engage its intended target?
disagreements.position: Yes — cortical amyloid load declined on PET and cerebrospinal fluid A β 42 and related APP metabolites fell by more than 60%, indicating the drug was acting at its intended target despite the absence of clinical benefit.
disagreements.quote: Taken together, these findings indicate that verubecestat was acting at its intended target.

disagreements.question: Is verubecestat associated with amyloid-related imaging abnormalities, as antiamyloid immunotherapies are?
disagreements.position: No. As in the previous trial, verubecestat was not associated with amyloid-related imaging abnormalities of the kind reported with antiamyloid immunotherapies.
disagreements.quote: As in the previous trial, verubecestat was not associated with amyloid-related imaging abnormalities that have been reported with antiamyloid immunotherapies.

trial_status_observation.status: Terminated early for futility — a decision to stop the trial was made in February 2018 at the recommendation of the data and safety monitoring committee, on the basis of futility of finding superiority for either verubecestat dose over placebo; enrollment had been completed and approximately 12 months remained before scheduled completion of part 1, and no patients completed the extension phase
